the study of the dynamics of the external ocular blood supply and its role in the pathogenesis of anterior segment ischaemic disease.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in man, centripetal blood flow is the rule in episcleral perforating arteries.
the anterior segment circulation is a complex, dynamic, and individualised network of arteries, arteriovenous shunts, and episcleral veins.
the anterior and posterior episclera are vascularised by separate but interrelated circulatory systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SAM is a useful tool for the investigation of the anterior segment circulation.
there is a rich and complex anterior segment circulation which is of considerable importance in ocular blood flow physiology, and that the SAM is a powerful and versatile tool for its investigation.
the SAM is the only technique to date which can reliably demonstrate the complex and variable flow patterns of the episcleral circulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SAM is the best way to image anterior segment blood flow and that the SAM can be used to investigate a wide range of clinical problems in the anterior segment.
the ocular blood supply is more complex than previously thought, with a large amount of blood flow going through the sclera.
